Thereafter, the applicant filed an application for execution.
It is the case of the applicant that a part of the compensation was paid by the respondents on 02.07.2013 and the remaining part of the compensation was paid on 15.05.2015.

Accordingly, the applicant filed an application for amendment in the execution application seeking interest on the delayed payment of compensation which was partially paid on 02.07.2013 and 15.05.2015.
However, by the impugned order dated 20.07.2024, the said application has been rejected by the trial court.

3. Challenging the order passed by the court below, it is submitted by counsel for the applicant that Executing Court has rejected the application on the ground that as per Article 125 of the Limitation Act, to record an adjustment or satisfaction of a decree, limitation is 30 days when the payment or adjustment is made.
It is submitted that as per Section 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the interest is to be paid till the compensation amount is actually deposited.

In the present case, as the trial court had not quantified the amount and had left it to be calculated by the Executing Court therefore the Executing Court is wrong in saying that the deposit of compensation without any interest on the delayed payment would amount to adjustment for satisfaction of the decree.
4. Per contra , the petition is vehemently opposed by counsel for the State.

However, it is submitted that the application filed by the applicant under Order VI Rule 17 CPC is barred by time and therefore it has been rightly rejected.
5. Heard learned counsel for the applicant.
6. Payment of interest on the delayed payment is the requirement of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

Therefore, the delay of everyday would give rise to fresh NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:20051 3 CR-983-2024 cause of action.

Under these circumstances, when there is a recurring cause of action and from joint reading of Section 23(1A), 31 & 34 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, it is clear that unless and until the entire compensation amount is paid, it cannot be said that the decree was satisfied or it was adjusted and therefore, the provision of Article 125 of the Limitation Act would not apply.
(Kindly see Harkaranjit Singh And Other vs State Of Haryana And Another decided on 16/10/2012 in CWP No.12786 of 2012).

sentences.text: 7. Under these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Executing Court committed a material illegality by rejecting the application filed by the applicant under Order VI Rule 17 CPC.
Accordingly, the order dated 20.07.2024 passed by X District Judge, Gwalior (M.P.) in Execution Case No.500022/2016 is hereby set aside.
The application filed by the applicant under Order VI Rule 17 CPC is hereby allowed.
8. Let necessary amendment be carried out within the period so stipulated by the Executing Court.

The Executing Court is directed to proceed further in accordance with law.
9.
With the aforesaid observation, this revision is allowed.
